Title: Monumenta Serbica spectantia historiam Serbiae, Bosnae, Ragusii (the title page in the OCR is read as Latin letters turned into Cyrillic lookalikes)
Creator: Franz Miklosich (Fr. Miklosich), editor; Vienna
Publisher: Vienna (Viennae): apud Guilelmum Braumüller; the OCR of the title page reads "ВИЕNNAE ... 1858"
Publication Date: 1858
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: pd-us-by-date. The OCR of the title page reads "1858" and the Braumüller imprint of Vienna; the title of the item itself ends "viennae-1858". The item record carries no date, creator, possible-copyright-status or licence field, so the title-page year is the only evidence.
Language: chu
Source: Internet Archive item monumenta-serbica-spectantia-historiam-serbiae-bosnae-ragusii-ed-f-miklosich-viennae-1858 (archive.org/details/monumenta-serbica-spectantia-historiam-serbiae-bosnae-ragusii-ed-f-miklosich-viennae-1858), full-text file monumenta-serbica-spectantia-historiam-serbiae-bosnae-ragusii-ed-f-miklosich-viennae-1858_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026. Host item uploaded without metadata. Three other scans of the same edition were opened and rejected: monumentaserbica00mikluoft (Cyrillic read as Latin noise throughout), monumentaserbic00miklgoog (Cyrillic read as wrong letters) and MonumentaSerbica (Cyrillic read as noise).
Provenance note: Header prepended; the host text follows unchanged. Nothing was normalised, stripped, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. OCR sampled at 5, 50 and 95 percent: the best of four scans, still poor. Cyrillic words are mostly recognisable but many letters are wrong (Latin and Greek lookalikes, yat and jer errors, capitals confused), and the front matter and the Latin editor's notes are garbled.
Content note: The standard 1858 edition of the medieval charters of Serbia, Bosnia and Ragusa in the Serbian recension of Church Slavonic, with Latin headings and notes. Bosnian rulers' charters and grants appear through the volume (for example the Ragusan privileges of the Radinović family near file lines 11240 and 12357, and a charter of Sultan Selim to Ragusa near 26384). The Bosnian Church's hierarchy appears in the witness lists, where the "djed" and the "gost" sign royal charters; this was not read here. SECOND WITNESS ONLY: do not quote from the OCR; locate a passage and read the page image. The Latin or German calendar of the same documents is better in Fermendžin (vendored) and Thalloczy-type collections (not found).
